patterns.usage_note: Picks up a label or claim just made, usually the speaker's own, and immediately cuts it down to size (社長とはいったって、社員は三人). The second clause is typically a scaling-down remark: only that much, hardly at all. This is the casual spoken end of the family; とはいっても is the neutral form safe in polite speech, and とはいえ and とはいうものの are the written siblings.

examples.ruby: 片付[かたづ]けたとはいったって、机[つくえ]の上[うえ]だけだよ。
examples.english: I say I tidied up, but all I did was the desk.

examples.ruby: ネットが安[やす]いとはいったって、送料[そうりょう]を足[た]せば店[みせ]と同[おな]じだよ。
examples.english: Sure, online is cheaper, but once you add shipping it comes out the same as the store.

examples.ruby: 毎日[まいにち]走[はし]るとはいったって、たった十分[じゅっぷん]だよ。
examples.english: I run every day, yeah, but only for ten minutes.

patterns.usage_note: Concedes the first clause as true, then states something that runs against the expectation it raises (春とはいえ、朝晩の冷え込みは厳しい). It attaches to a bare noun as readily as to a plain clause, and it also stands alone at the head of a sentence as a conjunction, 'Even so, …'. It is the most formal of the everyday members and is largely written: essays, editorials and careful speech, where speech would use とはいっても.

examples.ruby: 春[はる]とはいえ、朝晩[あさばん]の冷[ひ]え込[こ]みは厳[きび]しい。
examples.english: It may be spring, but mornings and evenings are still bitterly cold.

examples.ruby: 値段[ねだん]が下[さ]がったとはいえ、まだ手[て]が出[で]ない。
examples.english: The price has come down, but it's still beyond my reach.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]は一人[ひとり]で暮[く]らせるとはいえ、心配[しんぱい]は尽[つ]きない。
examples.english: My grandmother can manage on her own, and yet I never stop worrying.

patterns.usage_note: Takes up a claim already on the table, the speaker's own words, received wisdom or an official line, and reports that reality has not followed (経験があるとはいうものの、実務となると勝手が違う). It is very close to とはいえ in meaning, but is used in speech as well as writing, and it can trail off unfinished where とはいえ cannot (相談すればいい、とはいうものの…). Polite speech more often uses とは言いましても.

examples.ruby: 経験[けいけん]があるとはいうものの、実務[じつむ]となると勝手[かって]が違[ちが]う。
examples.english: I do have experience, but the moment it's the real work, nothing goes the way I expect.

examples.ruby: レシピ通[どお]りに作[つく]ったとはいうものの、味[あじ]は店[みせ]のとは別物[べつもの]だった。
examples.english: I followed the recipe to the letter, and yet what came out tasted nothing like the shop's.

examples.ruby: 近所[きんじょ]とはいうものの、歩[ある]けば三十分[さんじゅっぷん]はかかる。
examples.english: They say it's close by, but it's a good thirty minutes on foot.

patterns.usage_note: Concedes a stated position and then reports something that contradicts it, keeping ながら's 'while saying' force, so it typically exposes a gap between what is professed and what is actually done (引退するとはいいながら、今も現場に立つ). Stiff and overwhelmingly written: essays, columns and narration rather than conversation. For a plain factual concession, とはいえ reads far more naturally.

examples.ruby: 引退[いんたい]するとはいいながら、彼[かれ]は今[いま]も現場[げんば]に立[た]つ。
examples.english: For all his talk of retiring, he is still out there on the job.

examples.ruby: 不作[ふさく]の年[とし]だとはいいながら、今年[ことし]の柿[かき]は驚[おどろ]くほど甘[あま]い。
examples.english: A poor year for the crop, they call it, and yet this autumn's persimmons are astonishingly sweet.

examples.ruby: 反対[はんたい]だとはいいながら、結局[けっきょく]誰[だれ]も声[こえ]を上[あ]げなかった。
examples.english: They all professed to be opposed, and yet not one of them spoke up.

glosses: however much of a … it may be
patterns.usage_note: Concedes an extreme or authoritative case in order to deny it any exemption (国王とはいえども、法を超えることは許されない). The shape is classical, so it belongs to maxims, statutes, editorials and period narration rather than ordinary speech, and it is often reinforced by いかに or たとえ. It attaches to nouns and also to plain verbs and adjectives (いかに急ぐといえども).

examples.ruby: 一分[いっぷん]とはいえども、無駄[むだ]にはできない。
examples.english: Even a single minute is not ours to waste.

examples.ruby: 子供[こども]とはいえども、約束[やくそく]は守[まも]らねばならない。
examples.english: A child, no less than anyone else, must keep his word.

examples.ruby: 国王[こくおう]とはいえども、法[ほう]を超[こ]えることは許[ゆる]されない。
examples.english: Not even a king may place himself above the law.
